comparator.name: Dentistry (Tandheelkunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The University of Groningen's current Dentistry documents page publishes the linked 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (OER) as the governing bachelor regulation. Although the PDF's browser metadata title is 'concept', its running header identifies it throughout as the 2026-2027 Dentistry bachelor OER; the official documents page presents it as the current OER. Articles 3.6, 4.1 and 7.1 establish an ordinary three-year, 180-ECTS curriculum of 60 ECTS per year. All 29 listed components are compulsory and total 60+60+60=180 ECTS. Article 7.1 explicitly confirms that there are no tracks, no minor space and no electives, so the normalized generic Dentistry target has no route to select. The current programme page independently confirms a 36-month, 180-ECTS, Dutch-taught bachelor that integrates biomedical, behavioural and dental science with extensive technical-skills training and patient care. Practical procedures are first trained on artificial jaws and teeth; diagnosis and treatment begin in Years 2 and 3; the curriculum culminates in the Bachelor Clinic and scientific work.

exception.reason: The defining 180-ECTS curriculum is entirely compulsory and integrates oral and general health science, oral diseases, radiation protection, dental diagnosis and treatment, progressive professional and technical skills, and supervised care of real patients in the 12-ECTS Bachelor Clinic. The current UCR catalogue provides relevant biomedical science, psychology, public health and research methods, but no dentistry, oral anatomy or biology, cariology, periodontology, dental materials, restorative procedures, endodontology, dental radiography, preclinical simulation, treatment planning or supervised clinical dental care. A 24-course UCR programme could reproduce parts of the biomedical and behavioural context but would omit the profession-defining dental science, manual skills and patient treatment. It would therefore not be a defensible closest match.
exception.curriculumContext: The formally published 2026-2027 Groningen curriculum totals exactly 180 ECTS: 60 ECTS in each of three years, with no tracks, minor space or electives. Its 29 compulsory components progress from healthy-human and healthy-mouth science, prevention and simulated professional skills through compromised oral health, oral diseases and further clinical skills to dental radiation protection, diagnosis and restoration, advanced professional skills and a 12-ECTS supervised Bachelor Clinic. The OER makes the skills sequence prerequisite-dependent and requires completion of both second-year professional-skills components, oral healthcare in context and most second-year theoretical components before entry to the Bachelor Clinic.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned availability, disciplines, topics and methods. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity, HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide relevant biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and HCBPSYC313 Advanced Research Seminar provide public-health, behavioural and research perspectives. None of the 151 courses teaches oral anatomy or biology, cariology, periodontology, dental biomaterials, restorative technique, endodontology, dental radiology, dental care planning, preclinical operative skills or supervised treatment of dental patients. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Dentistry programme.
